title: Crypto padding and integer byte representation
oracle: Padding expectations use known constant prefix bytes and a reviewed final-byte length table. Valid tail amounts preserve the known prefix; zero preserves the tail. Native Buffer radix conversion and BigInt.asUintN supply independent representation oracles instead of the source shift/OR algorithm. Hex expectations use literal bytes and each enumerated integer; malformed hex expectations are fixed reviewed constants. No implementation output generates expectations.

execution.results: Both revisions pass all 11,874 probes with unchanged comparison. Four executable tests pass. No real crypto provider operation is exercised.

exclusions: Strict PKCS#7 validation is not the source contract: zero padding, inconsistent pad bytes and amounts above a block size may be accepted.
Returned padding view aliases the original buffer in source; JSON byte snapshots cannot prove alias identity or mutation propagation.
